acceptance_criteria.criterion: A test verifies that fetching /test?key=value&foo=bar causes the matched handler to receive a URLSearchParams with the expected entries (key=value, foo=bar).
A test verifies that fetching /test (no query string) causes the matched handler to receive an empty URLSearchParams.
A test verifies that a noBody: true route handler receives undefined as the body argument.
A test verifies that a route with statusCode: 204 returns HTTP 204 with an empty body.
A test verifies that a handler throwing ApiError returns the mapped status code and error JSON.
A test verifies that a handler throwing a generic Error returns HTTP 500 with INTERNAL_ERROR code and that process.stderr.write was called.
Tests use a real createServer() / fetch pattern (no synthetic IncomingMessage/ServerResponse mocks).

summary: Created mcp-server/tests/gui/dispatch-route.test.ts exercising dispatchRoute() in isolation via a real createServer()/fetch test pattern with synthetic Route arrays. All six acceptance-criteria scenarios are covered: query-parameter injection (AC-2), empty URLSearchParams for no query string (AC-3), noBody:true yields undefined body (AC-4), statusCode:204 returns HTTP 204 with empty body (AC-5), ApiError thrown maps to correct status and error JSON (AC-6), generic Error returns HTTP 500 with INTERNAL_ERROR and calls process.stderr.write (AC-7). All 6 tests pass.

summary: Reviewed dispatch-route.test.ts against all four review dimensions: Maintainability, Best Practices, Performance, and Future Context. The implementation is clean and well-architected. The startDispatchServer helper uses a real createServer()/fetch pattern with ephemeral port 0 to eliminate port-collision risk, which is correct and future-proof. comments.note: Added a clarifying comment to the unreachable .catch() branch in startDispatchServer (dispatch-route.test.ts lines 46–52). The branch is unreachable because dispatchRoute() catches all handler errors internally (ApiError, PayloadTooLargeError, generic Error) and always resolves its returned Promise<boolean>. Without the comment, a future contributor modifying dispatchRoute's error-propagation contract would have no signal that this safety-net branch's reachability assumption would be violated. Non-behavioral change — no test logic modified.

AC-7 stderr assertion uses .toMatch(/server/) which matches both the [server] prefix written by dispatchRoute and the [test-server] prefix written by the startDispatchServer .catch() branch. Since the .catch() branch is unreachable in this test, the assertion is behaviorally correct, but the broad regex would also pass if the .catch() branch fired unexpectedly. QA also noted this. Consider pinning to /\[server\]/ in a follow-up to distinguish production stderr from test-harness stderr.
